correctness.rationale: PASS. For H arbitrary finite m-vertex graph and transitive Γ acting on the K_r coordinate, the vertex orbits in H□K_r are exactly the r-vertex clique fibers. Any geometric Γ-fixed point has equal barycentric coordinates within each fiber; orbit-barycenter simplices yield a PL homeomorphism compatible with k-inclusions. For S of base vertices, an independent set in S×[r] takes at most one vertex per fiber, and color labels of chosen vertices give a proper r-coloring of the selected induced subgraph. Conversely any r-coloring gives an independent set, proving α(G[S×[r]])=b_r(S). This exact identity yields the full fixed filtration {S:b_r(S)<k}. If χ(H)≤r then b_r(S)=|S| and each stage is simplex (k−2)-skeleton, whose standard Morse matching gives wedge C(m−1,k−1)S^{k−2}, including k=2 discrete m points and k>m contractibility. At k=m, proper S always qualify and full S qualifies iff H is not r-colorable, giving sphere/ball dichotomy; persistence bar lengths follow since neighboring reduced degrees differ. The original verifier enumerates all labeled graphs m≤4 for r=2,3 and targeted larger cases, direct invariant faces and Euler identities; finite checks are corroboration, not the proof.

originality.rationale: PASS, best of knowledge. Kim–Lew defines complexes with bounded graph independence number and establishes collapsibility estimates but does not classify Γ-geometric-fixed filtrations on H□K_r. Filakovský's 2026 robust-clique paper analyzes ordinary homotopy of grids and square-sequence graphs, not pointwise fixed complexes of clique-fiber transitive actions or the colorability terminal criterion. Resultary's equivariant Euler-character work gives alternating homology traces on bipartite graphs (different object/invariant), not the exact PL fixed orbit model. The elementary coloring correspondence may have an unnoticed equivalent formulation in graph-theoretic literature; this is a qualified priority risk, not evidence of coverage.
